name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle031
definition_title: Positive reporting masks, terminal completions, and retained source data
natural_language_statement:
Fix natural microblock parameter $h$, block count $J$, a global output $q$, and a reporting depth $k$. The positive-child index list selects exactly those enumerated children whose original raw-prefix count is positive. For a list of parent prefixes, the partial accumulation is the ordered concatenation of the positive children of the first parents. The positive-expansion program constructs children, performs physical catalog lookup and exact queries, selects positive results, and gathers aligned left/right mask arrays; below its scratch boundary only those output intervals may change.

A terminal completion chooses exactly $(J-k)h$ of the remaining output coordinates. Its two full endpoint masks combine that subset and its complement with the fixed prefix endpoints. The associated pair mass is the product of the independently trimmed left and right original-input histogram counts. The terminal work expression sums the actual bucket-test costs over the unchanged enumeration order; each test charges physical selected pairs rather than the entire Cartesian product.

The bundle also defines a closed source-control host program and its literal procedure records, along with finite source-control costs. Its retained-data predicates record computed controls, contiguous original-index buckets and source-transform banks for the same normalized B/C lists. The normalization predicate exposes the three strictly increasing lists, equality of their represented value sets with the color classes, band tables, owner records, and flattened A-incidence arrays. A selected-color prime wrapper reads dimensions from those normalized headers; a result writer stores the compact eight-cell result after retained source data.

These definitions preserve original raw incidences and their multiplicities while turning abstract positive frontiers and terminal completions into physical mask arrays. They support exact cost charging and reuse of the same normalized witnesses throughout the complete deterministic integer 3SUM proof.

name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle032
definition_title: Physical frontier layout and terminal reporting contracts
natural_language_statement:
The frontier-step program reads each stored parent mask pair, executes the complete positive expansion and appends its positive children to aligned output arrays. For a finite raw-incidence set $I$ and wanted label $w$, write $m_0$ for its raw-prefix mass at depth zero and $G(h)$ for the local child count. The allocated frontier capacity is

$$\operatorname{capacity}(I,w)=(m_0+1)G(h).$$

A slot contract stores the exact frontier length, residual query mask, and left/right prefix-mask arrays at each depth. Terminal interfaces define full endpoint hashes and independent trim flags in the exact completion order, together with the literal batch cost and original-value hit predicate. The prepared-terminal program builds these endpoints and flags and scans only their selected physical bucket products.

The finite source host has explicit original-size time, space, finish-address and word budgets. Its normalized-data contract retains the normalized color arrays, band headers, owner records and actual flattened A-incidence count. The source constructor reads its destination and every cover pointer from previously written headers, computes the J-fold modulus, and invokes the complete shared source host.

The dense-stop mass of a visited wanted-label list is the sum of its root raw masses; this definition supports cumulative stopping before proportional traversal. For the level loop, a catalog record contains switch parameter, box cutoff and box/index/pointer bases. Its storage contracts specify sorted prefix codes, exact box pointers, local transformed box values, and complete source transforms. Separate bounds place every retained array below the ownership boundary, while scratch constraints cover enumeration masks, Pascal/power tables, remainder computation, lookup magnitudes and all queried values.

These definitions are the concrete memory and resource interfaces used by the complete deterministic integer 3SUM reporting loop. The stored catalog supplies data for an actual query program rather than assuming a query oracle, and the physical frontier retains the original combinatorial order.
